1 Data Preparation

The GBSG breast cancer dataset (survival::gbsg, N = 686) is prepared identically for both the Cox and Poisson-offset analyses.

df.analysis <- survival::gbsg
df.analysis$id <- seq_len(nrow(df.analysis))
df.analysis$grade3 <- as.integer(df.analysis$grade == "3")

confounders.name <- c("age", "meno", "size", "grade3", "nodes", "pgr", "er")
outcome.name     <- "rfstime"
event.name       <- "status"
treat.name       <- "hormon"
id.name          <- "id"

cat("GBSG: N =", nrow(df.analysis),
    ", events =", sum(df.analysis[[event.name]]),
    sprintf("(%.0f%%)\n", 100 * mean(df.analysis[[event.name]])))
#> GBSG: N = 686 , events = 299 (44%)

2 Cox Survival Analysis (Reference)

This is the standard ForestSearch analysis from the primary vignette.

fs_cox <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis,
  confounders.name = confounders.name,
  outcome.name     = outcome.name,
  treat.name       = treat.name,
  event.name       = event.name,
  id.name          = id.name,
  # Threshold parameters (per León et al. 2024)
  hr.threshold           = 1.25,
  hr.consistency         = 1.0,
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.80,
  stop_threshold         = 0.80,
  # Search configuration
  sg_focus             = "hr",
  max_subgroups_search = 3,
  use_twostage         = TRUE,
  # Factor selection
  use_grf                    = TRUE,
  return_selected_cuts_only  = TRUE,
  use_lasso                  = TRUE,
  cut_type                   = "default",
  # Subgroup constraints
  maxk   = 2,
  n.min  = 60,
  d0.min = 12,
  d1.min = 12,
  # Consistency evaluation
  fs.splits = 100,
  # Sequential for load_all() compatibility
  parallel_args = list(
    plan         = "sequential",
    workers      = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  ),
  # Output options
  showten_subgroups = TRUE,
  details           = TRUE,
  plot.sg           = TRUE
)

3 Poisson-Offset GLM Analysis (Sanity Check)

The Poisson regression with log(rfstime) as offset approximates the Cox model when the baseline hazard is locally constant. Under this approximation, exp(log-IRR) should track the Cox hazard ratio, and the identified subgroup should be similar or identical.

The key API difference: outcome.name is the binary event indicator, offset.name points to the follow-up time column, and outcome_type = "binary" with effect_measure = "IRR".

NoteGRF and LASSO not yet wired for GLM outcomes (Phase 1)

The Poisson-offset analysis disables GRF and LASSO candidate selection because these components use causal_survival_forest() and glmnet(family = "cox") respectively, which require survival-specific inputs. Wiring causal_forest() and glmnet(family = "poisson") is Phase 3 work. For now, all confounders are cut at quartiles/median (the cut_type = "default" path).

fs_pois <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis,
  confounders.name = confounders.name,
  conf_force = c("er <= 0"),
  outcome.name     = event.name,        # binary event indicator (0/1)
  event.name       = event.name,        # same column (binary IS the event)
  treat.name       = treat.name,
  id.name          = id.name,
  # GLM outcome specification
  outcome_type     = "binary",
  effect_measure   = "IRR",
  offset.name      = outcome.name,      # "rfstime" — log(rfstime) used as offset
  # Threshold parameters — same as Cox for comparability
  # IRR thresholds map directly to HR thresholds
  hr.threshold           = 1.25,        # log(1.25) screening on log-IRR scale
  hr.consistency         = 1.0,         # log(1.0) = 0 consistency threshold
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.80,
  stop_threshold         = 0.80,
  # Search configuration
  sg_focus             = "hr",
  max_subgroups_search = 3,
  use_twostage         = TRUE,
  # Factor selection — GRF/LASSO not yet wired for GLM (Phase 1)
  use_grf   = FALSE,
  use_lasso = FALSE,
  cut_type  = "default",
  # Subgroup constraints
  maxk   = 2,
  n.min  = 60,
  d0.min = 12,
  d1.min = 12,
  # Consistency evaluation
  fs.splits = 100,
  # Sequential for load_all() compatibility
  parallel_args = list(
    plan         = "sequential",
    workers      = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  ),
  # Output options
  showten_subgroups = TRUE,
  details           = TRUE,
  plot.sg           = FALSE              # KM plots not applicable for GLM
)

3.1.2 Candidate Subgroups from Search

Show code 
pois_cands <- fs_pois$find.grps$out.found$hr.subgroups
if (!is.null(pois_cands) && nrow(pois_cands) > 0) {
  # HR column contains log-IRR in the GLM path; exponentiate for comparison
  pois_cands$IRR <- exp(pois_cands$HR)

  factor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(pois_cands),
    c("grp", "K", "n", "E", "d1", "m1", "m0", "HR", "L(HR)", "U(HR)", "IRR")
  )

  cat("Top candidates (sorted by IRR):\n\n")
  top <- head(pois_cands[order(-pois_cands$IRR), ], 10)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(top))) {
    active <- factor_cols[
      as.numeric(unlist(top[i, factor_cols, with = FALSE])) == 1
    ]
    cat(sprintf("  #%d: log-IRR = %6.3f  (IRR = %5.2f)  n = %3d  %s\n",
                i, top$HR[i], top$IRR[i], top$n[i],
                paste(active, collapse = " & ")))
  }
} else {
  cat("No candidates found\n")
}

Show code 
# ITT-level comparison of Cox log-HR vs Poisson log-IRR
cat("\nITT-level effect estimates:\n")
#> 
#> ITT-level effect estimates:
Show code 
cox_itt <- survival::coxph(
  survival::Surv(rfstime, status) ~ hormon, data = df.analysis
)
pois_itt <- glm(
  status ~ hormon, family = poisson(link = "log"),
  offset = log(rfstime), data = df.analysis
)
cat("  Cox  log-HR: ", round(coef(cox_itt)["hormon"], 4), "\n")
#>   Cox  log-HR:  -0.364
Show code 
cat("  Pois log-IRR:", round(coef(pois_itt)["hormon"], 4), "\n")
#>   Pois log-IRR: -0.3556
Show code 
cat("  Difference:  ", round(coef(pois_itt)["hormon"] - coef(cox_itt)["hormon"], 4), "\n")
#>   Difference:   0.0084
NoteInterpreting the Comparison

The Cox and Poisson-offset paths may identify different subgroups for two reasons:

  1. Candidate factor sets differ. The Cox path uses GRF + LASSO for variable selection; the Poisson path uses quartile cuts only (Phase 1). This means the Cox path evaluates a smaller, more targeted set of candidates.

  2. The Poisson approximation is imperfect. The GBSG data has a Weibull-like hazard (not constant), so the Poisson log-IRR diverges slightly from the Cox log-HR, especially in subgroups with heterogeneous follow-up.

Despite these differences, the ITT-level estimates should agree closely, and the identified subgroups should share common factors (particularly estrogen receptor status, which is the dominant prognostic/predictive variable in this dataset).

When GRF and LASSO are wired for GLM outcomes (Phase 3), the candidate sets will align and the comparison will be tighter.
